title: An exact burst-count null needs exchangeable intervals, and nucleus labels give little held-mouse gain in 9,941 thalamic units
abstract: We derived the exact finite distribution of burst-spike counts under uniform interval permutation for a long-interval then short-run rule. The law matches all 29,523 ternary sequences of lengths 1 to 9. Independent intervals with block-varying distributions gave global-shuffle rejection fractions of 9 to 100 percent in four selected conditions. Shuffles within the true blocks gave 3 to 7 percent. This shows that shuffle excess cannot by itself identify a local burst mechanism. We also tested published burst statistics for 9,941 IBL thalamic units from 97 mice in 27 nuclei. Nucleus means reduced held-mouse squared error by 0.70 percent with unit weighting but increased it by 1.41 percent with mouse weighting. No nucleus passed an exploratory Holm-corrected test of mouse means. Some nucleus rank information remained in disjoint mouse halves. These results limit a strong claim about nucleus-specific burst order; they do not refute the raw burst gradient or estimate causal wiring effects. Raw interval category counts are absent from the source tables, so the new exact law could not be applied to each IBL unit. Code, compatible input tables, proof and results are included.

display.caption: Exact burst-count probabilities and permutation-test rejection fractions for independent interval draws. The changing-distribution conditions violate global exchangeability. True blocks are known in this simulation.
Mouse-level nucleus estimates and held-mouse prediction gains. Intervals are uncorrected mouse-bootstrap intervals. No nucleus passed Holm correction in the separate exploratory t tests.
